description:
Informer and propagandist Ilya Remeslo, who recently left a psychiatric hospital, revealed how he ended up there after sharply criticizing Vladimir Putin.
 The Z-blogger gave an interview to Ksenia Sobchak, in which he stated that on March 18, ambulance workers arrived at his home accompanied by police.
 “They came in and said point-blank that your texts are stirring up society, there is public outrage… That is, they didn’t ask how I was feeling, what my state of mind was, and so on. They were exclusively interested in my texts about Vladimir Putin.”
 When asked who had called the ambulance, Remeslo declined to answer, citing medical confidentiality. He also dismissed the theory that relatives had tried to shield him from potential liability for his words.
 According to the blogger, he initially refused to sign consent for hospitalization, but after three days signed it retroactively. In the hospital, Remeslo claims he was prescribed quetiapine and lithium. He also stated that he does not regret his statements.
 Remeslo said he stopped supporting Putin after Yevgeny Prigozhin’s mutiny, and that he feels guilt toward Alexei Navalny.
 “In my defense, I can say that I did everything to prevent his return to Russia. When it became known that he might return, I proposed a theme to the Presidential Administration: ‘You don’t need problems with him, do you? Let’s intimidate him. I’ll write another piece, based on donations. If he returns, this will definitely be carried out.’ The Administration approved all of this. \[…\] One could understand that I was not a simple person — I had contacts and capabilities. I even wrote to Navalny’s people: don’t let him return, there will definitely be a trial here.”
 At the end of the interview, when asked how he would like to be represented in the media, Remeslo said he wants to be called the “head of an opposition movement” in Russia.
 Ilya Remeslo runs a blog where he regularly criticized the opposition, published denunciations, and supported the Russian authorities. In mid-March, he published a post in his Telegram channel listing his reasons for no longer supporting Putin.
 Additionally, Remeslo confirmed to ASTRA that he had received money from the Presidential Administration to provoke and undermine the non-systemic opposition, in particular Alexei Navalny. **He also claimed that 99% of Z-military bloggers share his view and believe Putin should step down.*\*
 After this, the informer was sent to a psychiatric hospital.
 Source: https://t. me/astrapress/110937

description:
Trump says ships blocked in Hormuz to be freed on Monday

    
US President Donald Trump says vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz will be allowed to leave from Monday morning.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he had instructed US officials to prioritise the safe passage of ships and their crews.
“I have told my Representatives to inform them that we will use best efforts to get their Ships and Crews safely out of the Strait,” he said.
Trump added that US representatives are engaged in “very positive discussions with the Country of Iran”, suggesting the talks could produce broader outcomes.
He described the move as a “humanitarian gesture on behalf of the United States, Middle Eastern Countries but, in particular, the Country of Iran”, noting that “many of these Ships are running low on food”.
Trump also warned that any interference with the operation would be met with force. He said those who attempt to disrupt the effort “will have to be dealt with forcefully”.
title: Trump says ships blocked in Hormuz to be freed on Monday

description:
Palestinian man killed by Israel as his wife was giving birth

    

Mourners in Nablus have laid to rest 26-year-old Naif Firas Ziad Samaro after Israeli forces shot him during a raid on the city, according to Palestinian officials.
The funeral took place in the occupied West Bank unfolded alongside a deeply personal tragedy. Samaro’s wife was in labour, giving birth to their child at the same time his body was being carried through the streets.
The Palestinian Ministry of Health said Samaro died after Israeli forces shot him in the head during the raid. Four others were wounded by live fire, including injuries to the chest and pelvis, while two children were also among the wounded.
The Palestine Red Crescent Society said Israeli forces also blasted dozens to tear gas, with 40 people affected and 10 taken to hospital.
During the funeral, Nablus Governor Ghassan Daghlas said the killing would not weaken Palestinians’ resolve, calling for unity in the face of continued Israeli attacks.
title: Palestinian man killed by Israel as his wife was giving birth

description:
The longer the Iran war goes on, the greater the impact on inflation, the US central bank warns

    
Neel Kashkari has warned that a prolonged war involving Iran could fuel inflation and damage the US economy, limiting the Federal Reserve’s ability to guide interest rate policy.
Speaking on CBS’s “Face the Nation”, Kashkari said he is closely watching the conflict and its impact on prices and demand, particularly as the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted.
The waterway, a key corridor for roughly a fifth of global oil and gas flows, has seen severe disruption during the war, driving up energy costs worldwide.
The conflict, which began after US President Donald Trump and Israel launched strikes on Iran on 28 February, has already pushed global energy prices higher, adding pressure to an already fragile inflation outlook in the United States.
Kashkari said the uncertainty surrounding the war complicates the central bank’s response and could force policymakers to tighten monetary policy.
“I don't feel comfortable signaling that a rate cut is in the cards. You know, we might be in worse scenarios, we might have to go the other direction,” he said.
Kashkari also broke with the majority at the latest Federal Open Market Committee meeting, joining a larger-than-usual group of dissenters who opposed the wording of the Fed’s policy statement.
title: The longer the Iran war goes on, the greater the impact on inflation, the US central bank warns

description:
Three people have died on a cruise ship in the Atlantic, the WHO said Sunday, one a confirmed case of hantavirus – an illness usually transmitted to humans from rodents.
The outbreak occurred on the MV Hondius, travelling from Ushuaia in Argentina to Cabo Verde, formerly known as Cape Verde.
“To date, one case of hantavirus infection has been laboratory confirmed, and there are five additional suspected cases,” the WHO told Agence France-Presse.
